[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Environment Variables, Secrets, and Masking in GitHub Actions"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Managing configuration data, credentials, and sensitive information securely is a critical part of any CI/CD pipeline. GitHub Actions provides robust mechanisms to handle environment variables, store encrypted secrets safely, and automatically mask sensitive data in your workflow logs."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Environment Variables in GitHub Actions"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Environment variables allow you to pass configuration settings into your steps. You can define them at the workflow level, job level, or step level using the env keyword."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"name: Environment Variables Example
on: [push]

env:
  GLOBAL_VAR: "Available to all jobs"

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      JOB_VAR: "Available only to this job"
    steps:
      - name: Print Variables
        env:
          STEP_VAR: "Available only to this step"
        run: |
          echo "Global: $GLOBAL_VAR"
          echo "Job: $JOB_VAR"
          echo "Step: $STEP_VAR""},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Using Encrypted Secrets"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Secrets are encrypted environment variables that you create in your repository, organization, or enterprise settings. They are never exposed in workflow logs. To use a secret, you reference it using the secrets context."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"name: Deploy Application
on: [push]

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout Code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Authenticate and Deploy
        env:
          API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.PRODUCTION_API_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          echo "Deploying with token..."
          ./deploy.sh --token "$API_TOKEN""},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Automatic Secret Masking"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"GitHub automatically redacts any registered secret that appears in the workflow logs. If a secret value is printed to standard output, it is replaced with three asterisks (***)."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Secrets are masked automatically if passed via environment variables or the secrets context."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Masking applies to strings longer than 3 characters to prevent accidental masking of common words like 'the' or 'and'."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Manual Secret Masking"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Sometimes dynamic tokens or sensitive data are generated at runtime and are not stored in GitHub Secrets. You can manually instruct the runner to mask these values using the add-mask command."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"name: Dynamic Masking Example
on: [push]

jobs:
  generate-token:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Generate Dynamic Password
        id: dynamic
        run: |
          PASSWORD="SuperSecretPassword123"
          echo "::add-mask::$PASSWORD"
          echo "MY_PASSWORD=$PASSWORD" >> $GITHUB_ENV

      - name: Use Masked Password
        run: |
          echo "The password is $MY_PASSWORD"
          # Output in logs will show: The password is ***"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Security"},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Never print secrets directly or implicitly in echo statements for debugging."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Scope secrets to specific environments (like production or staging) rather than repository-wide when possible."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Regularly rotate tokens and secrets stored in your repository settings."}]
